title: The number index: every quantity this site recomputed, and where it came from

body.md: Every figure below was computed from the paper's own tables before being written, and each row names the card that did the work. Nothing in this index is a quotation from the paper's prose unless it is marked as one. Use it two ways: as a lookup when you want a value without reopening a table, and as a checklist if you want to verify this site against the paper yourself.

body.md: **The two quoted gains in Section V-B are $5.86$ and $2.28$.** The nearest reproducible quantities are $5.656$ and $2.119$. The abstract's "average improvement of 2.5%" matches neither and states no comparison target. All three quoted values are recorded in the ledger, card 112, entries 2 and 3.

body.md: **All panel readings are approximations from the plotted curves**, accurate to roughly half a gridline of the vertical axis, which is about one point. The $\beta = 1$ gap and the ordering of the four noise curves are robust to that error; individual point values are not. Where this card gives a number the paper also states, the two agree except for the $\beta$ gap, where the text's "approximately 10" and the read-off $9.5$ are the same claim.

body.md: **How to use this index when you read the paper yourself.** Pick any row, open the table it names, and reproduce the value. If you match, the row was right and the index is doing its job as a shortcut. If you do not match, you have found either an error here or a cell whose reading is ambiguous — and either is worth knowing before you cite anything from this page. **The index is checkable on purpose: it is the one part of this site that makes a claim about a number in isolation from any argument, and a claim like that should always come with the means to falsify it.**
